 Hon'Ble Vikas Budhwar, J.

Heard Sri Ritesh Srivastava (AoR A/R 1302/12) holding brief of Ms. Rafeeqa Anees khan, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Pankaj Kumar Rai, learned State Law Officer for the State.
2.

This application u/s 528 of BNSS has been preferred to quash the Summoning Order dated 20.12.2024 in Complaint Case No.7459 of 2023 (Smt. Renu Prakash Vs. Virendra Kain & others)
under Section 85, 115(2), 352 B.N.S. and Section 3/4 of D.P.Act, Police Station-Pilkhuwa,
District-Hapur, pending in the Court of Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hapur.

sentences.text:
3. The case of the applicants is that on 12.05.2023 proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. came to be lodged by the opposite party no. 2 wife against the applicants who are husband, father-in-law,
Jeth and Jethani for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 406, 307, 354B, 377 IPC read with Section 3/4 of DP Act with an allegation that the marriage of the opposite party no. 2 stood solemnized with the applicant no. 1 on 11.02.2024 at the time of marriage, huge expenditure were incurred to the tune of Rs. 7,00,000/- and gifts were also offered but the demand of the applicants was much more as they demanded Rs. 10,00,000/- cash and a Honda City Car, however, on 22.10.2018, the opposite party no. 2's parents arranged an amount of Rs. 1,30,000/- and offered to the applicants and with the wedlock, a baby was born on 19.06.2018.

However, the applicants were not happy and again the demand of dowry was made on 26.09.2021 and not only in the said behaviour but also abuses were hurled and thereafter on 10.10.2021 again maltreatment was meted and the opposite party no. 2 was subjected to violence and assault and on 09.04.2024 again, the demand of dowry was being made.

Post recording of the statements 200 Cr.P.C. on 03.05.2024 followed by of Prakash Chandra on 28.05.2024 and Gautam Kumar on 19.07.2024, the applicants came to be summoned on 20.12.2024 under Sections 85, 115(2), 352 BNSS read with Section 3/4 of the DP Act.

Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for the simple reason that first of all, the complaint stood preferred on 12.05.2023 and the allegations and the offences which have been mentioned in the proceedings under Section 156(3) are pre-enforcement of the BNSS which came into effect on 01.07.2024.
He submits that even the proceedings stood lodged under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., thus, the summoning order insofar as it summons the applicants under the provisions of BNSS cannot be sustained.

He further submits that even otherwise, he seeks to rely upon a decision of the Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 12287 of 2024 (Deepu & 4 others vs. State of U.P & 3 others) decided on 06.08.2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 12287 of 2024 (Deepu & 4 others vs. State of U.P & 3 others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that even otherwise the allegations contained in the complaint are omnibus, general and they are not specific and though the applicants came to be summoned under the provisions of Sections 115(2) but there is no injury report available on record.

It is also contended that there is no question of any demand of dowry as there are no instances mentioned and further the court below in a routine manner without recording any prima facie satisfaction has summoned the applicants and further the statements of the witnesses are tailor-made and they are interested witnesses.
He seeks to file discharge application.

4. Learned State Law Officer, on the other hand, submits that from the perusal of the statements made under Sections 200 and 202 vis-a-vis the nature of the allegations contained in the complaint Virendra Kain And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162963046/

sentences.text: there are no material contradictions or variations which go to the root of the matter, thus, the case becomes triable, however, he submits that though the applicants have been summoned under the provisions of BNSS but that would not invalidate the order.
5. I heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

6. Considering the submissions so made across the bar as well as the stand of the counsel for the applicant as per instructions and the nature of allegations as well as overall fact situation, the application stands disposed of granting liberty to the applicants to prefer discharge application by 26.09.2025 and on the said motion, the court below shall decide the same strictly in accordance with law without granting unnecessary delay.

7. Till the discharge application is decided, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in Summoning Order dated 20.12.2024 in Complaint Case No.7459 of 2023 (Smt. Renu Prakash Vs.
Virendra Kain & others) under Section 85, 115(2), 352 B.N.S. and Section 3/4 of D.P.Act, Police Station-Pilkhuwa, District-Hapur, pending in the Court of Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Hapur.
